description: Rebuild the species page experience (species/*.html + species-page.js/css) as an academic-grade scrollytelling narrative with cinematic design, structured around the 7-section content architecture: Hero moment, The Science, On Screen, The Methodology, Root Causes (COM-B), The Evidence, and References. Each species page should feel like a mini-documentary with rich academic content, proper citations, and the new cinematic dark design language.
steps: 1. Rewrite src/species-page.js to render the new 7-section content architecture from the enriched JSON data: a) Hero moment - species name with large cinematic typography, hero image (from hero_image field or TMDB backdrop), IUCN status badge, and the hero_stat (one devastating statistic displayed prominently). b) The Science - taxonomy table (GBIF-aligned: kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species), population data, IUCN status, habitat range with country list, key locations. c) On Screen - every relevant film/documentary with: title, year, TMDB link (clickable), poster image, classification badge (documentary/fiction/educational), narrative technique badge, brief overview. Group by classification. Include a note about how this connects to RQ2. d) The Methodology - how this species data connects to RQ1-RQ4, citing Rose's visual methodology (with proper citation format), explanation of the analytical framework used. e) Root Causes (COM-B) - structured as three columns: Capability barriers, Opportunity barriers, Motivation barriers, explaining why this species is threatened through the behaviour change lens. Cite Michie et al. 2011. f) The Evidence - what research shows about media coverage correlating with conservation outcomes for this species. Reference relevant academic papers. g) References - full academic citation list in consistent format (Author, Year, Title, Journal/Publisher).

2. Rewrite src/species-page.css with the cinematic dark design language matching the main page: a) Dark background (#0a0a0f base), cream/white text. b) Sections separated by generous spacing and subtle horizontal dividers. c) Hero section: full-width hero image with dark gradient overlay, species name in massive cinematic type. d) Cards/panels: dark semi-transparent backgrounds with subtle borders, no glassmorphism. e) TMDB media cards: dark cards with poster images, clean typography, clickable links styled distinctly. f) COM-B section: three-column layout with distinct colored headers (capability=blue, opportunity=green, motivation=amber). g) Reference list: academic formatting, hanging indent style. h) Responsive: single column on mobile, multi-column on desktop. i) Film-grain texture overlay consistent with main page.

3. Update species/*.html template (all 10 files follow same pattern as tiger.html): ensure they reference the correct script path and have correct data-species attributes. The HTML structure stays minimal since content is rendered by JS from JSON data.

4. Ensure the species-page.js correctly handles the new JSON structure gracefully - if a field is missing (e.g., evidence_summary), skip that section rather than crashing. The page should work with both old and new JSON formats during transition.
acceptance_criteria: npm run build succeeds with the new species page code
The species page JS renders all 7 content sections when data is available
TMDB media entries show clickable TMDB URLs, classification badges, and narrative technique labels
The COM-B section displays three distinct columns for capability, opportunity, and motivation barriers
Academic references are displayed in proper citation format
The 4 Research Questions are referenced in the methodology section with species-specific relevance notes
The design uses dark/cinematic styling consistent with the rebuilt main page
Pages degrade gracefully when optional fields are missing from JSON
verification: Run `npm run build` and confirm it succeeds without errors
Check that dist/species/ contains all 10 HTML files
Inspect the built species-page JS bundle to confirm it references all 7 section renderers
